metadata.purpose: Small human-readable golden example set for demos and regression checks
metadata.warning: Synthetic patients, draft LLM-reviewed labels, not clinical gold, not for clinical use

cases.short_rationale: Patient has confirmed idiopathic PD with motor symptoms and uses levodopa. No exclusion criteria identified for a lower-extremity exercise trial.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Simple eligible case. PD diagnosis is the sole operative criterion and is clearly met. Good regression anchor for the most common include path.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has advanced PD with motor fluctuations on levodopa. Age 70 meets the 45-70 range. Consistent with inclusion criteria for a safety/tolerability study.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Eligible case where both age and disease severity criteria are explicitly matched. Tests numeric age boundary (70 = upper limit) and advanced-stage logic.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has confirmed idiopathic PD, age 62 within the 50-80 range. No exclusion criteria identified for a blood pressure and tyrosine supplementation study.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Clean eligible case with explicit age range match. Useful for verifying that idiopathic PD inclusion and numeric age rules fire correctly together.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has PD with freezing of gait, which is directly relevant to a lower-extremity exercise trial. No exclusion criteria identified.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Eligible case where a specific motor symptom (FoG) aligns with the trial focus. Tests that symptom-positive patients are not incorrectly blocked.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has early-onset PD without advanced disease markers. The trial requires advanced PD severity. Age 45 is within range but disease stage does not qualify.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Not-eligible case where age criterion passes but disease severity fails. Tests that the matcher does not conflate age eligibility with overall eligibility.

cases.short_rationale: Cognitive impairment with low MoCA score meets the exclusion criterion for a cognitive/neuropsychiatric protocol requiring intact cognition.
key_trial_criteria: Trial excludes patients with dementia or cognitive impairment
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Not-eligible case driven by a cognitive exclusion. Tests that the exclusion rule fires correctly when cognitive impairment is documented. Common and important pattern.

cases.short_rationale: Cognitive impairment with low MoCA is a standard exclusion for DBS surgical trials due to neuropsychiatric risk.
key_trial_criteria: Trial excludes patients with dementia or cognitive impairment
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Not-eligible case where cognitive exclusion applies in a DBS surgical context. Shows the cognitive exclusion rule generalises across trial types.

cases.short_rationale: Suspected parkinsonism with unclear final diagnosis does not meet the confirmed idiopathic PD inclusion requirement for this trial.
key_patient_facts: Diagnosis not confirmed as idiopathic PD
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Not-eligible case where diagnostic uncertainty results in exclusion. Contrasts with Cases 9 and 10 where diagnostic uncertainty produces unclear rather than not_eligible.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has PD and frailty. Frailty may affect ability to participate in a pragmatic exercise trial but no explicit exclusion for frailty is stated in the protocol.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Unclear case driven by an unresolved safety signal. Frailty is present and potentially relevant but not explicitly excluded. Tests whether the matcher flags comorbidity ambiguity.

cases.short_rationale: Patient has an implanted cardiac pacemaker. Acoustic stimulation devices may be contraindicated with pacemakers, but this is not confirmed in the trial summary.
cases.why_this_case_is_useful: Unclear case driven by a device safety signal. Pacemaker presence is clinically meaningful in a stimulation device trial but the protocol does not explicitly address it. Important pattern for device trial coverage.
